artifacts.why: The +3.0 trend z is driven almost entirely by the final 11-09 00h block (value 1.0 vs herd 0, dev +20) which is a near-empty few-minute end-of-coverage block, plus a single 11-08 12h spike. Base desync_share is actually normal (16% vs 17%, z -0.1). The trend deviation is a coverage/edge artifact, not a sustained drift.

Flank-amplitude z of +2.7 (161%) is contradicted by a normal, low breath rate of 23/min from 7 valid windows and no distress posture; the amplitude is inflated by very close bunk windows (large box pixel scale), not true effort.

final.behavior_assessment: I do NOT believe the two biggest drivers. The desync_share__trend spike is an end-of-coverage artifact (near-empty final block), and the elevated breathing_effort amplitude is not corroborated by rate or posture. Appetite is intact: feed_response shows COW_10 reaching the bunk promptly at major herd rushes (0-7 min, latency 14.9 vs 19.1 min) and staying as long or longer (18-27 min), with more but shorter visits (rate 1.5 vs 1.1/h explains the shorter 6.5-min visits). Longer lying bouts and slightly more isolation are mild and within noisy short-coverage range. Overall behavior looks largely normal for a top-ranked-by-score but clinically unremarkable cow.
final.summary: COW_10 ranks #1 on the behavior score, but the score is inflated by two artifacts: a desync 'trend' spike from a near-empty final block, and an elevated breathing-effort amplitude that is contradicted by a normal breath rate (23/min) and no respiratory distress. Appetite, feeding, and posture at the bunk all look normal. No action needed beyond routine observation; if anything, pen-ride to get a clean standing head view to rule out nasal/ocular discharge, which the cameras could not assess.
